movimento: Sentado no voador, com o glúteo no assento, as costas (o glúteo e a parte de cima das costas) encostadas no encosto, a cabeça na linha do tronco e os pés chapados no chão, um pouco mais abertos que o quadril; o assento regulado para os pegadores ficarem na altura dos ombros, um pouco abaixo. Segura os pegadores verticais com a pegada neutra (polegares para cima) e a mão fechada, com os braços abertos para os lados, os cotovelos levemente dobrados, um pouco abaixo dos ombros e apontando para trás, e as mãos na linha dos ombros. Fecha os braços na frente do peito num arco largo, como num abraço, sem mudar o ângulo dos cotovelos, até as mãos quase se encostarem (no fim os cotovelos apontam para os lados); volta devagar pelo mesmo arco até as mãos chegarem de novo na linha dos ombros, sentindo o peito alongar, sem levar os braços muito para trás. Os braços da máquina giram em volta de eixos verticais em cima dos ombros e os pegadores acompanham as mãos. O tronco, as escápulas, a cabeça, o quadril e os pés ficam parados (as costas não saem do encosto no fim).

cinesiologia.plano: transverso: adução horizontal do ombro na ida (fecha os braços) e abdução horizontal na volta, com o braço um pouco abaixo da horizontal; cadeia cinética aberta
cinesiologia.articulacoes: ombro (adução horizontal na ida, abdução horizontal na volta, em rotação interna: o cotovelo aponta para trás com os braços abertos e para os lados com os braços fechados); cotovelo parado, levemente dobrado (~20°); punho quase reto; escápulas paradas no encosto; quadril, joelhos e tornozelos parados, com os pés no chão
cinesiologia.agonistas: peitoral maior, porção esternal (ExRx: Target "Pectoralis Major, Sternal"), em contração concêntrica na ida e excêntrica na volta
cinesiologia.sinergistas: peitoral maior (porção clavicular), peitoral menor, deltoide anterior, bíceps braquial (cabeça curta) e serrátil anterior (ExRx: Synergists "Pectoralis Major, Clavicular", "Pectoralis Minor", "Deltoid, Anterior", "Biceps Brachii, Short Head", "Serratus Anterior"; na página de 2026 entra também "Coracobrachialis"); a eGym lista como principais "Pectoralis major", "Pectoralis minor" e "Deltoid" e como secundários "Biceps brachii" e "Coracobrachialis"; no estudo patrocinado pelo ACE o pec deck ativou o peitoral maior 98% do supino com barra ("Both the pec deck (at 98% of muscle activation compared to barbell bench press)...")
cinesiologia.estabilizadores: bíceps braquial e braquial seguram o cotovelo no mesmo ângulo e os flexores do punho seguram o pegador (ExRx: Stabilizers "Biceps Brachii", "Brachialis", "Wrist Flexors")
cinesiologia.fases: concêntrica (fecha os braços até as mãos quase se encostarem — NSCA: "Pull the handles toward each other with a slight bend in your elbows until they touch"; Hoist: "bring your hands together in a sweeping arc until they are almost touching") e excêntrica (volta devagar até sentir o peito alongar — ExRx: "Return to back toward original position until mild stretch is felt in chest or shoulder"; NSCA: "Let the handles return outward to the starting position"; eGym: "Return to the starting position in a controlled motion")

referencias: ExRx.net — Lever Seated Fly (https://exrx.net/WeightExercises/PectoralSternal/LVSeatedFly, lido na cópia do Internet Archive de 21/11/2023; o site responde 403 direto; na cópia de 29/07/2026 a mesma página virou "Lever Isolateral Seated Fly", com a mesma preparação e o mesmo fim da execução): "Utility: Auxiliary", "Mechanics: Isolated", "Force: Push"; Preparation: "Sit on machine with back on pad. Grasp handles to both sides, shoulder height. Slightly bend elbows and internally rotate shoulders so elbows are back."; Execution: "Keeping elbows pointed high, push lever handles forward and together. Return to back toward original position until mild stretch is felt in chest or shoulder. Repeat."; Comments: "Shoulders are kept internally rotated so elbows are pointing out to sides. The starting position of levers can be adjusted on many apparatuses, allowing for both rear delt and chest to be exercised."; músculos: Target "Pectoralis Major, Sternal", Synergists "Pectoralis Major, Clavicular", "Pectoralis Minor", "Deltoid, Anterior", "Biceps Brachii, Short Head", "Serratus Anterior", Stabilizers "Biceps Brachii", "Brachialis", "Wrist Flexors" (a de 2026 põe também "Coracobrachialis" nos sinergistas). A versão com almofadas nos antebraços é outra página (Lever Seated Fly (gripless): "Position both arms behind padded levers").

NSCA — Exercise technique (Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning), no resumo do Achievable CSCS, cap. 15 (https://app.achievable.me/study/cscs/learn/exercise-technique-for-free-weight-and-machine-training-exercise-list-part-3 e ...-fundamentals-of-exercise-technique, lidos em 07/10/2026): Pec deck (machine) — "Sit with five-point contact."; "Grasp the handles with a closed, neutral grip."; "Align your midchest with the handles."; "Pull the handles toward each other with a slight bend in your elbows until they touch."; "Let the handles return outward to the starting position." (o resumo lista como músculos "Pectoralis major, anterior deltoids, triceps brachii" — o tríceps não entra aqui: o cotovelo fica parado); posição de 5 pontos: "Head on the bench or pad", "Shoulders/upper back on the bench", "Buttocks on the bench or seat", "Right foot flat on the floor", "Left foot flat on the floor"; pegada neutra: "Neutral grip - knuckles point laterally (like a handshake)"

eGym (fabricante) — Smart Strength, M13 Butterfly e M14 Butterfly Reverse (https://knowledge.egym.com/en/smart-strength/work-out-on-smart-strength/exercises, lido em 07/10/2026): M13 — Primary muscles "Pectoralis major", "Pectoralis minor", "Deltoid"; Secondary muscles "Biceps brachii", "Coracobrachialis"; "Sit with your back straight against the backrest."; "Hold the handles between chest and shoulder height. Keep your elbows slightly bent."; "Start with your arms open to the sides until light tension is felt in the chest."; "Bring the handles together against the resistance. Keep your shoulders lowered and elbows slightly bent."; "Return to the starting position in a controlled motion."; M14 (o crucifixo invertido): "Sit upright and forward with your chest against the chest pad"; "Open your arms outward and backward against the resistance until the handles are in line with the shoulders."

Hoist Fitness (fabricante) — HD-3900 Pec Fly/Rear Delt (https://www.hoistfitness.com/pages/hd-3900-pec-fly-rear-delt, lido em 07/10/2026): "start by adjusting the seat height by releasing the pull pin and setting it so that when seated your feet are flat on the floor"; "Located directly above the seat and between each of the swing arms you will find the ROM (Range Of Motion) Adjustment."; "Sit facing away from the machine with your back in an upright position against the pad. Grasp one of the handles in each hand. In a smooth controlled motion with your arms at full extension being careful not to lock your elbows, bring your hands together in a sweeping arc until they are almost touching."; Rear Delt: "Sit facing the machine in an upright position with your chest against the pad."

ACE — ACE-sponsored Research: Top 3 Most Effective Chest Exercises (Schanke W, Porcari JP e colegas, Universidade de Wisconsin–La Crosse; https://www.acefitness.org/certifiednewsarticle/2884/ace-sponsored-research-top-3-most-effective-chest-exercises/, lido em 07/10/2026): "Both the pec deck (at 98% of muscle activation compared to barbell bench press) and the bent-forward cable crossover (93% of muscle activation) elicited nearly equivalent muscle activation as the barbell bench press."; no pec deck do estudo (o de almofadas nos antebraços): "Place your feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width (or wider) apart, and press your back firmly against the back pad.", "Slowly push the wings all the way toward the center until they are just about to meet." e o erro "will lift the upper back off the back pad to finish the motion"; no crossover: "some exercisers start with the shoulders in horizontal hyperextension or the arms behind the torso ... there is a risk of injury in the shoulder during hyperextension"

ACE — Lying Chest Fly (https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/21/lying-chest-fly/, lido em 07/10/2026; o mesmo movimento com halteres, deitado): "slightly flexing the elbows, but maintaining a neutral wrist position (avoid flexion/extension at the wrist joint)"; "Maintain your slightly flexed elbows, neutral wrist position"

Skelcore (fabricante) — What Makes A Pec Fly Machine Feel Natural And Safe? (https://www.skelcore.com/guides/what-makes-pec-fly-machine-feel-natural-safe, lido em 07/10/2026): "The primary job of a pec fly machine is to guide the arms through horizontal adduction, bringing them inward toward the body's midline."; "The arms should move smoothly inward without pushing the elbows excessively behind the torso at the starting position."; "When the machine's rotational axis aligns reasonably well with the user's shoulder area, the movement tends to feel fluid. When the pivot sits too high, too low, or too far behind the user, the handles may pull the arms through an unnatural path."

Precor — patente US4840373A, Four-bar rigid-drive variable resistance pectoral fly machine (Henry H. Maag; depositada em 24/03/1988, publicada em 20/06/1989; titular atual Precor Inc; https://patents.google.com/patent/US4840373A/en, lida em 07/10/2026): "A shoulder-joint horizontal-flexion exercise machine (pec-deck or pectoral fly machine) ... a pair of offset rigid counter-rotating assemblies which rotate on axes which are approximately common with the vertical axes through the operator's shoulder joints."; "apply resistive force to the same through circular paths about the vertical axes of rotation of the operator's shoulder joints"; "Present day pectoral fly machines all work on the same primary principle of fixing the positions of the operator's shoulder joints while applying resistive forces to the operator's upper arms which tend to make the upper arms rotate about their respective shoulder joints, through a transverse plane relative to the operator's upper body"

Medidas da máquina — Life Fitness Insignia Series Pectoral Fly/Rear Deltoid (https://www.lifefitness.com/en-us/catalog/strength-training/selectorized/insignia-series-pectoral-fly-rear-deltoid, lido em 07/10/2026): "The Insignia Series Pectoral Fly/Rear Deltoid is a two-in-one machine that replicates the body’s natural motion."; "Dimensions (L x W x H): 79.9" x 77.6" x 80.1" (203 cm x 197 cm x 203 cm)"

zonas.nome: glúteo e coxas sentados no assento
zonas.fonte: NSCA (Achievable CSCS) — posição de 5 pontos ("Buttocks on the bench or seat")

zonas.nome: costas (parte de cima, escápulas) no encosto
zonas.fonte: ExRx — Lever Seated Fly ("Sit on machine with back on pad"); eGym — M13 Butterfly ("Sit with your back straight against the backrest"); Hoist — HD-3900 ("your back in an upright position against the pad"); NSCA (Achievable CSCS) ("Shoulders/upper back on the bench")

zonas.nome: glúteo encostado na base do encosto
zonas.fonte: ACE — pec deck do estudo ("press your back firmly against the back pad"); ExRx — Lever Seated Fly ("Sit on machine with back on pad")

contatos.nome: no fim as mãos quase se encostam, sem encostar
contatos.fonte: Hoist — HD-3900 ("bring your hands together in a sweeping arc until they are almost touching"); NSCA (Achievable CSCS) ("Pull the handles toward each other ... until they touch"); ACE ("until they are just about to meet"). A cena deixa 2 cm entre a pele das 2 mãos

folgas.nome: braço esquerdo × braço direito do voador

eixos.nome: eixo do braço esquerdo do voador na vertical do ombro esquerdo
eixos.fonte: Precor, patente US4840373A de pec deck ("a pair of offset rigid counter-rotating assemblies which rotate on axes which are approximately common with the vertical axes through the operator's shoulder joints"); Skelcore ("When the machine's rotational axis aligns reasonably well with the user's shoulder area, the movement tends to feel fluid")

eixos.nome: eixo do braço direito do voador na vertical do ombro direito

angulos.nome: no começo o braço fica um pouco atrás da linha dos ombros (alongamento leve, sem passar muito)
angulos.fonte: ExRx — Lever Seated Fly ("Return to back toward original position until mild stretch is felt in chest or shoulder"); eGym — M13 Butterfly ("Start with your arms open to the sides until light tension is felt in the chest"); Skelcore ("without pushing the elbows excessively behind the torso at the starting position"); ACE (risco no ombro em "horizontal hyperextension"). Com o cotovelo dobrado, a mão fica na linha dos ombros

angulos.nome: no fim os braços fecham na frente do peito
angulos.fonte: ExRx — Lever Seated Fly ("push lever handles forward and together"); NSCA (Achievable CSCS) ("Pull the handles toward each other ... until they touch"). Com os ombros parados no encosto e as mãos quase se encostando no meio, o braço passa um pouco da frente (~93°)

angulos.nome: no fim as mãos ficam juntas na frente do peito
angulos.fonte: Hoist — HD-3900 ("until they are almost touching")

angulos.nome: braço na altura dos ombros, um pouco abaixo, o movimento todo
angulos.fonte: ExRx — Lever Seated Fly ("Grasp handles to both sides, shoulder height"; "Keeping elbows pointed high"); eGym — M13 Butterfly ("Hold the handles between chest and shoulder height")

angulos.nome: braço um pouco abaixo da horizontal (o cotovelo não cai)
angulos.fonte: ExRx — Lever Seated Fly ("Keeping elbows pointed high")

angulos.nome: antebraço na horizontal (a mão na altura do cotovelo)
angulos.fonte: ExRx — Lever Seated Fly ("Keeping elbows pointed high"; "internally rotate shoulders so elbows are back": o cotovelo dobra no plano em que o braço anda, não pra baixo)

ExRx — Lever Seated Fly ("Slightly bend elbows"); NSCA (Achievable CSCS) ("with a slight bend in your elbows"); eGym — M13 Butterfly ("Keep your shoulders lowered and elbows slightly bent"); Hoist — HD-3900 ("being careful not to lock your elbows")
ACE — Lying Chest Fly ("maintaining a neutral wrist position (avoid flexion/extension at the wrist joint)"); o que sobra (~6–8°) é o desvio de lado que o pegador vertical pede

angulos.nome: pegada neutra (pegador vertical, polegar pra cima, palmas viradas pra onde o braço anda)
angulos.fonte: NSCA (Achievable CSCS) ("Grasp the handles with a closed, neutral grip"; "Neutral grip - knuckles point laterally (like a handshake)")

angulos.nome: tronco parado, encostado e quase em pé
angulos.fonte: Hoist — HD-3900 ("your back in an upright position against the pad"); eGym — M13 Butterfly ("Sit with your back straight against the backrest"); encosto 5° atrás da vertical
eGym — M13 Butterfly ("Sit with your back straight against the backrest")

angulos.nome: escápulas paradas no encosto (os ombros não vão pra frente no fim)
angulos.fonte: eGym — M13 Butterfly ("Keep your shoulders lowered"); ACE (o erro "will lift the upper back off the back pad to finish the motion"); Precor, patente US4840373A ("Present day pectoral fly machines all work on the same primary principle of fixing the positions of the operator's shoulder joints")
a medida da fábrica é coxa × prolongamento do tronco pra baixo (90 − inclinação do tronco pra trás)

angulos.nome: joelhos a ~90°, pés chapados no chão
angulos.fonte: Hoist — HD-3900 ("setting it so that when seated your feet are flat on the floor"); NSCA (Achievable CSCS) ("Right foot flat on the floor", "Left foot flat on the floor")

angulos.nome: cabeça parada na linha do tronco, olhando pra frente
angulos.fonte: regra da fábrica (a cabeça não mexe); o boneco em pé, no repouso, mede ~−11° (tecnica3d.cabeca_tronco). A NSCA pede a cabeça no encosto ("Head on the bench or pad"), mas no boneco a nuca fica ~6 cm à frente da linha das costas e encostar pedia ~19° de pescoço pra trás, olhando pra cima: a cabeça fica perto do encosto, sem encostar
